subject: Post-call: Nova Labs inference sizing, target $/1M ask & startup credit request
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Anna Perez <anna@novalabs.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novalabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Nova Labs inference sizing, target $/1M ask & startup credit request

Anna / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Summary of what I took away from our discovery:
- Workload: customer-facing assistants + nightly batch reranks for search. Real-time generation is the critical path.
- Current pilot usage: ~200M tokens/month (predominantly generated tokens). Expected ramp to ~600M in 3 months and ~1.2B tokens/month at scale (6–9 months) if accuracy and latency targets hold.
- Latency target: 200–300ms p50 for interactive flows.
- Budget band (what you shared on call): $12k–$30k/month initially; finance wants a clear unit $/1M token target before committing to a longer term.
- Primary asks from your side: a pricing band showing committed-use options, what the startup program would cover (credits/waiver), and a multi-year incentive outline for 12–24 month pledges.

What I’m proposing as next steps (action owners in parens):
1) I’ll model a couple of committed-use scenarios and attach a short worksheet with unit economics across the ramp (see nova-inference-modeling-v1.xlsx). I’ll include a target $/1M row so you can see the implied monthly spend vs discount. (Markus)
2) Ben will draft a committed quote (PDF) that shows simple tiering: monthly token bands, % discount vs list, and an extra multi-year rebate line item. Ben — can you include an example 12-month and 24-month structure? (Ben)
3) Tom — can you confirm whether a 12-month financial commit requires PO or if a signed SOW will do for Nova’s procurement? If you prefer, we can produce both. (Tom)
4) We’ll reconvene next week for a 30-minute review once the draft quote is ready.

Notes on target unit economics you mentioned: you said the team would be comfortable in the low hundreds $/1M tokens if quality/latency are met (~$150–$300 per 1M). I’ll make sure the modeled scenarios surface that explicitly. If that target changes after you chat internally, flag it here and I’ll re-run the numbers.

Attachments: nova-inference-modeling-v1.xlsx (workload/ramp model)

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0178

From: Anna Perez <anna@novalabs.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novalabs.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Nova Labs inference sizing, target $/1M ask & startup credit request

Thanks Markus — clear notes, appreciate the model. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 200M/month today is a conservative estimate — the customer-facing assistant is small right now but will explode if latency and LLM quality are good. We built the budget assuming an aggressive growth curve, so the 1.2B/mo by month 6 is realistic.
- The $150–$300 per 1M token target is exactly the range we were hoping to see. Ideally we’d like to land closer to $150 if possible, but we’re open to committed tiers.
- Startup program: we are a Series A company (closed May 2027). Are we eligible for Redwood’s startup credits or is that limited to seed-stage? If eligible, what’s the typical credit size and is it applied to list pricing before discounts?

Tom — looping you for procurement questions (we may need a 12-month commit to get the pricing we want).

Anna

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Anna Perez <anna@novalabs.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novalabs.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Draft committed quote + startup credit guidance for Nova Labs

Hi Anna / Tom — attaching a short draft quote (draft-commit-quote-novalabs.pdf) and a quick summary in-line to accelerate review. I modeled three committed tiers and a startup program credit we can apply up-front:

Summary (high level):
- List baseline: $1,200 per 1M (example list for hosted generation + embedding blended).
- Tier A (entry commit): 250M tokens/month commit — net $420 per 1M (65% off list)
- Tier B (growth commit): 750M tokens/month commit — net $260 per 1M (78% off list)
- Tier C (scale commit): 1.25B tokens/month commit — net $220 per 1M (82% off list)
- Multi-year incentive: additional 10% unconditional rebate applied as an annual credit on year 2 for 24-month commitments (applies on net spend after discounts).
- Startup program: Nova Labs (Series A) qualifies for a one-time onboarding credit of $30k applied to initial 3 months; credit is applied to invoice after discounts.

Notes + assumptions:
- Net $/1M numbers above include both generation and auxiliary costs (prompt tokens + model overhead). I’ve kept the math intentionally conservative for tail costs.
- Discounts assume a billing/commit cadence where Nova prepays or commits to a monthly minimum billed monthly with quarterly reconciliation.
- If you require stronger SLOs/SLAs (custom SLO-backed latency or dedicated capacity), that can shift price by ~15–30% depending on GPU reservation needs — I’ve left that optional for now.

Attachments: draft-commit-quote-novalabs.pdf (PDF shows line items, payment terms, and optional SLO add-ons)

Next steps: if the Tier B/C math looks good to you, we can (a) convert draft into a formal SOW/quote and (b) put a 30-minute call on the calendar this week to sign off on the preferred commit window.

Best —
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0127

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novalabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Anna Perez <anna@novalabs.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft committed quote + startup credit guidance for Nova Labs

Thanks Ben — that’s helpful and a good starting point. A few quick procurement items from my side:

- Nova prefers a 12-month contractual commit with net-30 invoicing rather than upfront prepayment. Please include both options in the formal SOW (prepay discount vs monthly billed commit).
- For the startup credit, confirm that the $30k is an invoice credit (post-discount) and not a gross list deduction. If you can show both line items on the quote that would be ideal.
- We’ll need an appendix outlining the optional SLO-backed dedicated capacity (what you called \"SLO add-ons\") — CPU/GPU reservation, expected p50/p95, and the incremental spend estimate.

Once you send the formal SOW with both billing options and the SLO appendix, I’ll run it through procurement. If the Tier B math hits ~$260 per 1M as modeled, I think we can get internal approval for a 12-month commit.

Tom Ellis
CFO, Nova Labs
t.ellis@novalabs.com | +1 415-555-0199
